The main takeaway from our work is that

phylogenetic analysis of melatonin receptor nucleotide and protein sequences can provide a useful molecular framework for the classification of melatonin receptors, which can be used in conjunction with functional studies to further our understanding of the genetic relationships between melatonin receptor sub‐types.

the phylogenetic analysis of nucleotide and encoded protein sequences is a useful tool in the classification of melatonin receptor subfamilies and in determining the subtype status of melatonin receptor genes.

the phylogenetic analyses based on nucleotide and amino acid sequences of melatonin receptors provide useful insights in the classification of melatonin receptor sub‐types, and that the genetic relatedness of melatonin receptor genes may not be the sole criterion for the classification of melatonin receptor subtypes.
